§6Carbon Dioxide§f §aYour ZIRNOX needs this waste gas to keep from melting. More isn't always better though.§f §bCarbon Dioxide§f (CO2) is a polluting gas that occurs as a waste product in petrochemical and material refinement. Its one job is cooling the §bZIRNOX§f reactor, which can consume up to §e16,000 mB§f. §6Production§f:
§b• Chemical Plant§f, 1,000 mB Natural Gas → 1,000 mB CO2 (3s, 100 HE/t)
§b• Electrolysis§f, Alumina (200 mB) → 100 mB CO2 + Aluminium Powder + Fluorite
§b• Fractioning Tower§f, Coker Gas (100 mB) → 75 mB CO2 + 25 mB Aromatics
§b• Combination Oven§f, Limestone Powder → CO2 + Calcium Powder
§b• Pyrolysis Oven§f, Coal Tar → 1,000 mB CO2 + Fine Soot §6Key Uses§f:
§b• §eZIRNOX Coolant§f, the only real use; trial and error needed to find the ideal amount for your fuel load §ePS:§f The Chemical Plant route (Natural Gas) is simplest for bulk production. But remember, dumping in more CO2 doesn't mean more power, experiment with amounts for your specific setup.
